name: Urgent care clinic

pf.license.need: always: each clinician (physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, nurse) holds their own active license from the state's board
pf.license.who: each person; the clinic too where the state's form licenses urgent care or walk-in centers (a switch); the mobile team where the state's form licenses mobile medical units (a switch)
pf.license.ask: each person's license number and national provider number in their invite reply (or the owner sends them); the clinic's facility license, its lab certificate and any mobile unit permit from the owner
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.tests: tests run on site, even a rapid strep test, only under the clinic's lab certificate (a waiver for simple tests); X-rays only where the state's radiation rules are met (a switch)
pf.license.away: house calls, hotel and workplace visits only where the state's rules allow them; a mobile unit permit where the state's form asks for one (a switch); the place where the patient is decides which state's license counts
pf.license.video: a video visit only with a clinician licensed where the patient is during the visit (a switch from the state's form, with any compact or telehealth registration)
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking; every company in Rosie's chain signs one with Rosie
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it

pf.services.shape: a saved spot in today's line at the clinic: an estimated time, not an appointment, and sicker patients are seen first; walk-ins join the same line; tests or treatment are added in the room from the price list, with the patient's yes first; a house call or hotel visit is sent now with an arrival estimate, or booked in an arrival window; a video visit
pf.services.examples: the example businesses' own prices (Lee Urgent Care and Lee Mobile Care), not a standard; a plan pays its own fee, and the patient's share (a copay) is checked by the front desk

list.name: Illness or injury visit (a saved spot in today's line, or a walk-in)
list.price: $150 self-pay, or the plan's copay (the example: a $35 copay)
list.kind: one price; tests and treatment added in the room from the list
list.length: about 30 minutes in the room; the wait depends on the line
list.after: the copay at the front desk at check-in; a self-pay price at checkout, after any tests; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the clinic its own way

list.name: Rapid strep test
list.kind: one price, added in the room
list.length: 10 minutes, result before the patient leaves

list.name: Flu or COVID test
list.kind: one price, added in the room

list.name: Stitches for a simple cut
list.price: from $140, set in the room by the cut's length, with the patient's yes first

list.name: X-ray
list.kind: one price, added in the room

list.name: School, sports or work physical
list.length: 20 minutes, in the line like any visit

list.name: Video visit
list.where: online, counted as at the clinic
list.after: billed by the clinic its own way after the visit
list.note: only while the patient is where the clinician is licensed

list.name: House call or hotel visit
list.kind: one price; tests and treatment added at the visit from the list
list.where: at the customer's place (a home, a hotel room)
list.after: the office bills the plan its own way, then the patient for any share; a self-pay visit gets the bill Rosie texts when the clinician texts DONE
list.note: sent now when someone is on call, or the soonest arrival window

list.name: IV fluids at a house call
list.kind: one price, added at the visit

list.name: Workplace visit day (flu shots, work injury checks, work physicals)
list.price: set with the employer: per person, or billed to the employer
list.length: a morning or a day at the workplace
list.where: at the employer's place (the host's place)
list.after: the office bills the employer or each plan its own way
list.note: each worker books their own spot and fills their own forms on the secure page; the employer never sees health details

pf.services.capacity: the line: about 4 patients an hour for each clinician on shift; one patient per room; the mobile team: one patient per visit, one clinician
pf.services.line: estimates come from who's waiting and who's on shift; online spots stop at 7:30pm, the last walk-in is 7:45pm and the clinic closes at 8pm (the example clinic's hours: 8am to 8pm every day); a spot is held 15 minutes past its estimate; the desk can pause online spots or add time to every estimate by one text
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the patient is always there
pf.services.online: a video visit, counted as at the clinic; the check-in code is read out at the start

beforeTimes: for you, your child, or someone you help
which visit: the clinic's own visit types only (illness or injury, a test, a physical, a video visit), never a symptom typed into the AI
a health plan (its name only) or paying yourself
for a house call: the address, inside the travel area
afterTime: anything the clinic should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a hotel or workplace visit: the room or the place to meet, and the front desk's rule for visitors
securePage: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the plan card
the reason for the visit, health history, medicines and allergies
the patient's own doctor, and an OK to send the visit notes there
consent to treat and the privacy notice
an OK to get texts about the spot, and if an interpreter is needed
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent, legal guardian or another adult with legal authority for anyone under 18 (every text goes to that adult, and the record says who booked); a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; a minor alone only for care the state's rules let a minor consent to (a switch)
pf.questions.neverAsked: symptoms, reasons and results are never asked or typed in the AI chat; the danger questions are put to the patient, and the AI never answers them for the patient

stop.words: chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs (a drooping face, a weak arm, trouble speaking, a sudden severe headache), heavy bleeding, fainting or a seizure, or someone who can't wake up
stop.say: Call 911 now, or go to the nearest emergency room. Don't wait in an urgent care line, and don't drive yourself.
stop.booking: no spot saved; the same words come first if they appear in any later message, and a saved spot is kept unless the patient gives it up

stop.words: swallowed something poisonous, or too much of a medicine
stop.say: Call Poison Help now at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if they're not awake or not breathing.
Call or text 988 now. If you're in danger, call 911.

goOn.words: a sore throat, a fever, a cough, a sprain or a small cut, with no danger words
goOn.what: matched to the clinic's own visit list from the patient's own words; Rosie never says how serious anything is or what care is needed

pf.safety.neverWait: a message with danger words is never told to wait in the line, and wait texts never suggest waiting instead of calling 911
pf.safety.names: an urgent care is never called an emergency room in any message, where the state's rules forbid it (a switch), and Rosie says it nowhere
pf.safety.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.name: Health forms and consent
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; finished while the spot is saved, or at the front desk on arrival
steps.who: every patient; a parent or guardian for a child
steps.result: not done before arrival: signed on the secure page at the desk before the patient is seen

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand, right away for a visit today
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered (the copay), some services only, not covered (the self-pay price), or can't check now (the desk checks at check-in); the spot stays either way

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; given on request, in the time the federal rules set
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

pf.first_steps.prep: arrive about 10 minutes before the estimate; bring a photo ID and the plan card; for a house call: someone to open the door, and the medicine bottles at hand

pf.visit.checkIn: at the clinic: the check-in code at the front desk, where the desk checks the photo ID and the plan card against the secure page; at a house call or hotel: the code from the patient at the door; a video visit: the code read out at the start
pf.visit.line: a booked time today, not a live line (the master has no live line): a sicker patient may be seen first, so a time can slip; a delay is texted as the master's running-late steps say
pf.visit.changes: tests, X-rays or stitches are added in the room from the price list, with the patient's yes first; results are given before the patient leaves; the clinician sends the patient to the emergency room if needed, and the clinic decides that, never Rosie
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the clinician's notes, results and discharge papers stay in the clinic's own records and patient portal, never in Rosie or a text; visit notes go to the patient's own doctor only with the patient's OK from the secure page
pf.visit.ownDoctor: the clinic tells the patient to follow up with their own doctor; Rosie never contacts another practice on its own, and the patient's AI can book that visit if the patient asks
pf.visit.away: the mobile clinician brings a kit with tests and IV fluids; no X-rays at a house call

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking, ever: no card saved, no hold, no deposit, at the clinic or away
pf.money.plans: the plans the clinic takes (its own list, set at sign-up); only the plan's name is asked at booking; the front desk checks coverage by hand right away for a visit today, and the spot stays either way; the copay is an estimate from that check
pf.money.selfPay: the posted self-pay prices are shown before the patient says yes; a self-pay patient is told while booking that they can ask for a written price estimate, and gets it on time
pf.money.after: at the clinic: the copay at check-in, a self-pay price at checkout after any tests, the clinic's own way; a balance after the plan pays, and a video visit, are billed by the clinic its own way, not by Rosie's text; a house call: the office bills the plan its own way, then the patient for any share; a self-pay house call or hotel visit: Rosie texts the bill
pf.money.fees: none: no fee to give up, move or miss a spot, for anyone (the example clinic's choice); where a clinic turns a fee on, never for patients whose plan or the state's rules bar one (a switch)
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.emergency: in a declared emergency, the self-pay prices don't go up where the state's rules limit prices (a switch)
pf.money.caps: fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules

pf.messages.never: texts to the patient carry only the clinic's name, the date, the estimated time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, symptoms, medicines, the reason, results or children's details; the mobile clinician's first name stays in house-call texts, for the door check
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the patient's initials only (A.M., never Alex M.) and carry no health details: those stay on the secure page
pf.messages.wait: wait texts describe the line, never the patient, and never suggest waiting instead of calling 911
pf.messages.symptoms: a patient's words about symptoms or a medical question are never saved as a note or passed on by text; Rosie points to the clinic's phone, or 911 for an emergency
pf.messages.results: results and medical questions go to the clinic's phone or its own patient portal, never through Rosie
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish; an interpreter asked on the secure page is passed to the clinic
pf.messages.minors: a child's texts go to the parent or guardian who booked; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
pf.messages.decider: for an adult who can't consent, the texts go to the person who decides

pf.staff.licenses: each clinician's own license, per state: physicians, physician assistants and nurse practitioners see patients; nurses and medical assistants help; the front desk checks in and takes payments
pf.staff.skills: every clinician on shift sees illness and injury visits; stitches and X-ray reads by the clinicians trained for them; only clinicians cleared for house calls go out with the mobile kit
pf.staff.supervision: a physician assistant or nurse practitioner works with a supervising or collaborating physician as the state's rules require (a switch): on site, or on call; the line opens only while a clinician who may see patients alone, or with the physician on call, is on shift
pf.staff.onCall: the mobile team keeps one clinician on call during its hours, with a backup; a sent-now visit goes to the on-call clinician first
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs prices over $500 and closing the line early; the desk may pause online spots and add time to the estimates
pf.staff.standIn: a clinician out at the clinic: Sam names the cover, and nobody's spot moves unless the line closes; the mobile clinician out: the backup clinician, or new times
pf.staff.closing: no clinician to cover: the owner closes the line by text; every saved spot is cancelled with no fee, and each patient is told to look elsewhere, or to call 911 for an emergency

pf.rules.records: medical records are kept by the clinic for as long as the state's rules require; a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the clinic's records
pf.rules.copies: a patient's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.showLicense: licenses shown where the state asks; where the state's rules require it, a notice when no physician is on site (a switch)
pf.rules.postedPrices: posted self-pay prices where the state's rules require them (a switch); everywhere, the price before the yes
pf.rules.noTurnAway: spots are never hidden or filtered by the kind of plan; where the state's rules forbid turning people away by plan type, that rule is on (a switch)
pf.rules.interpreter: free language help where the clinic's funding or the state's rules require it (a switch); asked on the secure page
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a minor, and what a minor may consent to alone (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.host: a workplace visit day only under the employer's written OK on file; the employer never sees a worker's health details
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form

pf.edges.lineMoves: the line grows (sicker patients first, or the desk adds time): every saved spot gets its new estimate by text, with Keep or Give up; no reply keeps the spot, since it's only an estimate
pf.edges.lateArrival: held 15 minutes past the estimate; later, the next open estimate with the patient's OK; no reply keeps the spot until the hold ends
pf.edges.noShow: not there 15 minutes after the estimate: the spot is released, with no fee
pf.edges.closesEarly: no clinician to cover: the line closes, every saved spot is cancelled with no fee, and walk-ins are told at the door
pf.edges.paused: the line is full: online spots pause, and walk-ins are still seen until the last walk-in time
pf.edges.worse: a later message with danger words gets the 911 words first, and the spot is kept unless the patient gives it up
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about medicine or symptoms gets the clinic's phone, never advice, and isn't saved
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: the self-pay price, or give up the spot with no fee
pf.edges.child: a child is seen only with the parent or guardian who booked, or an adult they named on the secure page
pf.edges.urgent: house calls are sent now to the on-call clinician, with the soonest window when nobody is on call; the clinic's line is never sent now
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way

story.A: Sam Lee, a physician, signs up two companies by text. Then on Sat Oct 24 at 9:30am, Alex asks an AI for a visit this morning at Lee Urgent Care and books 11:00am. A sicker patient may be seen first, so the time can slip. The desk checks Alex's plan by hand, the health forms stay on the secure page, and Alex pays the $35 copay at the front desk. Pick a money choice at the top to follow its path.
story.B: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then on Thu Oct 22 at 6:40am, Alex, too sick to drive, asks an AI for a house call. Lee Mobile Care sends Ravi, the nurse practitioner on call, now: he checks in at Alex's door at 19 Birch Ln about 8:20am. The office bills Alex's plan its own way. Pick a money choice at the top to follow its path.

Refit Tue Oct 27 2026 (R12) to the REDESIGN 2 master: facts planbill, forms, sentnow, results, extrawork, children, video; sensitive on; no $2 (S1-62 off); arrive setstart (A) and window (B). The live line was cut from the master (D66 #1), so flow A now books a set time this morning (sicker patients may go first); the old line words are gone. Money A list|none|counter only (Urgent care visit, $150 self-pay; the $35 copay in the example). Money B list|none|own (main) and list|none|bill (House call $179). No fee anywhere. Every old words op is gone (the record and the homes word money, contact and fees). The home company is now Lee Mobile Care (word limits).
Pilot: dentist (from). Urgent care runs like the dentist: plans checked by hand at the front desk, the patient's share paid there, health forms only on the secure page, no $2 for a health practice. What differs: a spot in today's line instead of a set appointment, so flow A rewords the master's saved time as an estimate that moves; and the house call uses the master's sent-now steps, as the locksmith does for lockouts. Nothing of the dentist's rename list was copied except its no-$2 sentences, with the words changed to urgent care.
Names: Sam Lee, a physician, owns Lee Mobile Care LLC (the master's main company: house calls and hotel visits as mobile care, plus workplace care; 640 Main St) and Lee Urgent Care LLC (the second company: the walk-in clinic, 75 Market St). Pat stays the office manager. Riley and Avery became Marcus (physician assistant) and Nadia (nurse practitioner) at the clinic; Jordan and Casey became Ravi (nurse practitioner, on call weekdays) and Luis (physician assistant, the backup). Alex lives at 19 Birch Ln. The master's license numbers got medical letters (MD, NP, PA, UC, MU).
Flow A story: Sat Oct 24, 9:30am. Alex wakes with a sore throat and a fever and asks an AI to save a spot in this morning's line. The estimate is about 11:00am (the master's own visit time). Spot saved 9:37am, the 'almost your turn' text 10:20am, check-in 10:50am, in a room 11:05am, paid 11:40am, rating 4:00pm. Every A7 what-if was re-timed into that morning.
Flow B story: Thu Oct 22, 6:40am. Alex, too sick to drive, asks for a house call. Sent now: Ravi on call takes it at 6:47am, texts OMW at 7:40am, checks in at 8:20am (the master's own check-in time), DONE 9:10am. The set-window branches stay for windows booked ahead and workplace days; B7-01 and B8-02 carry no clock (a different booking), and B8-01 is Luis's 8am day list.
Money A: list|none|counter only. Nothing is ever taken before; the copay ($35 in the example) at check-in, a self-pay price ($150) at checkout after any tests; tests and X-rays added in the room from the list with a yes; a balance after the plan pays and a video visit are billed by the clinic its own way. No card path: the clinic charges no fee to give up or miss a spot.
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (the office bills the plan its own way, then the patient for any share). list|none|bill is a self-pay house call or hotel visit ($179), with Rosfield's bill at DONE. A plan's share is the office's own bill, so B9-19's 'Insurance pays part' branch is off (reviewer, Oct 23). No hold, card, deposit or full price: nothing is taken before a house call, and there's no trip fee.
Sign-up: Sam taps 3 (own way) at S1-15 for plan visits, then sets self-pay visits to the bill. S1-13, S1-14, S1-16, S1-18, S1-42, S1-45, S1-46 and S1-57 say nothing is taken before and no fee. The clinic's Stripe waits (S1-49), since nothing goes through Rosie there.
The line (flow A): A4-14 shows estimates, A4-15 picks one (by name, waitlist and taken-time branches off), A4-19 is 'online spots paused', A6-11 is 'the line moved a moment ago', A7-01 is the 'almost your turn' text (renamed), A7-14 is 'The line slows down' (renamed from 'Riley runs late': the desk texts LINE +30 and every spot hears its new estimate), A7-70/A7-73 hold a spot 15 minutes then offer a later estimate, A7-22 closes the line early with no fee, A3-32/A3-20/A3-21 are walk-ins in the same line. Spots name no clinician, so A7-59, S11-87 and S11-90 take the no-name branches in flow A; flow B's house calls are by name.
Safety and privacy: the AI puts the danger questions to the patient (A3-22); chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, heavy bleeding get 911 or the ER at once, never a wait (A3-24, A7-13, B3-19, B7-17). Rosie never says how serious anything is (A3-26, B3-21). Patient texts carry only the business, the time, the place (and in flow B the clinician's first name, for the door check): no visit type, plan, symptoms, tests, results or children's details. Plan check results go by secure link (A7-49, A7-50, B4-53 to B4-56, B7-44). Owner and staff texts use initials and no health details. Exam notes and results stay in the clinic's own records and portal (A8-23, A8-45, A10-22, B8-18, B8-44, B10-19).
A parent or guardian books for a child (A4-25, A4-70, B4-46) and stays; a child without a parent's consent isn't seen (A8-51, B8-54).
Requests never wait for Sam's OK: S11-03 is off in both flows, and A6-01's and B6-03's 'Sam's OK first' and 'An expert reads' branches are off. The S11 quote example is a group of work physicals (A, $720) and a flu shot day (B, $640, the master's own number). S11-08's color quote, S11-13's BLOCK, S11-55 and S12 examples were reworded to the line or to house calls.
Shared sections: S2-06, S2-10, S2-19 and S2-20 differ by flow (the master names Riley or Jordan, Jules or Jesse), so their words ops are flow-specific. S1-58/S1-59's visit days are Lincoln High School's sports physicals in A and Riverside Plant's flu shots in B.
Plug-in splits kept whole: A8-02 (something to bring); B4-81, B7-55, B8-58 (house calls sent now, windows booked ahead). Every other plug-in split turns its unused branches off.
Off as never used: repeat plans, packages, gift cards, contracts, damage holds, crews, set dates, minimums, classes, drop-offs, waitlists, the landlord, bank transfer, tips, the cancel period for care given (B10-05's refund branch), 'Alex runs late' at a house call, items left, rented or sent to a shop (B8-72).
Kept words: none. The fill option copies a words op's text onto the master's hidden money variants of S1-42, S1-46, S1-47 and B7-01, so hidden paths read the same.
Not sure (for the reviewer): the video visit is billed the clinic's own way on the counter path, not by Rosfield's bill, to keep flow A to one money path; A7-14 reuses 'Riley runs late' for the line slowing; a desk command 'LINE +30' and 'CLOSE today' are words, not master commands; the 30-minute stand-in wait in B7-19 stays the master's.
Reviewer (Oct 23): the 911 list adds a sudden severe headache, fainting and a seizure; A7-13's 911 text says not to wait for the spot. S1-54 and S1-65 say nothing is taken and no $2 is paid. Owner and staff texts use A.M. throughout. The not-our-work examples are an MRI (A4-38) and an X-ray at home (B4-03), not dental work. B3-01's live line is off. S12-24 flags a suspect number for Sam instead of waiting for his OK, since no request waits for Sam here. S11-21's list names LINE and CLOSE. B8-33's late text goes to Dana, Ravi's next patient.
